# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QH (Cave 1), Col. 10 | **Condition:** Better preserved

---

**10:1** What is flesh compared to these things? And what is a creature of clay that it should accomplish great wonders?

**10:2** For it abides in iniquity from the womb, and in faithless guilt until old age.

**10:3** I know that righteousness does not belong to a mortal, nor perfection of way to a son of man.

**10:4** To God Most High belong all righteous deeds; and the way of man is not established.

**10:5** Except by the spirit that God fashioned for him, to make the way blameless for the children of man.

**10:6** That all His creatures may know the power of His might and the fullness of His mercies upon all the children of His favor.

**10:7** As for me, trembling and dread have seized me, and all my bones have shattered.

**10:8** And my heart has melted like wax before the fire, and my knees have dissolved like water poured upon a slope.

**10:9** For I have recalled my acts of guilt together with the faithlessness of my forefathers.

**10:10** When the wicked rose up against Your covenant and the wretched against Your word.

**10:11** Such is one in iniquity from the womb, and in faithless guilt until old age.

**10:12** For I said, in my transgression I have been cast out from Your covenant.

**10:13** But when I remembered the might of Your hand together with the fullness of Your mercies.

**10:14** Then I rose and stood firm, and my spirit was strengthened to withstand affliction.

**10:15** For I have relied upon Your covenant-faithfulness and the fullness of Your compassion.

**10:16** For You make atonement for iniquity, to cleanse humanity from guilt by Your righteousness.

**10:17** Not for the sake of man do You act, but for the sake of Your glory.

**10:18** For You — You have fashioned both the righteous and the wicked.

**10:19** And who can stand before You when Your judgment falls?

**10:20** And what is one born of woman that he should be reckoned as righteous?

**10:21** I know that righteousness does not belong to a mortal, nor perfection of way to a son of man.

**10:22** To God Most High belong all righteous deeds, and the way of man is not established.

**10:23** Except by the spirit that God fashioned for him.

**10:24** And You have formed all the works of the earth and the ordinance of all their tasks from before eternity.

**10:25** And You have created the peoples for their appointed service and a host of spirits for Your dominions.

**10:26** You have assigned their duty for all the ages and the verdicts of their appointed seasons.

**10:27** For You have fixed their decrees from before the ages, and the work of every [...] You have laid out before You.

**10:28** The ways of man in all his deeds [...] You have laid out before You.

**10:29** And it is known by the wisdom of Your knowledge that You determined their course from before eternity.

**10:30** And apart from You nothing is accomplished. And nothing is known without Your will.

**10:31** To God Most High belong all righteous deeds; and the way of man is not established except by the spirit that God fashioned for him.

**10:32** And You have fashioned the breath for the tongue, and You know its words.

**10:33** And You have ordained the fruit of the lips before they came into being.

**10:34** And You set words upon a measuring-line, and the expression of the breath of the lips by measure.

**10:35** And You bring forth sounds according to their mysteries, and the outpourings of breath according to their computation.

**10:36** To declare Your glory and to recount Your wonders in all the works of Your truth.

**10:37** And the judgments of Your righteousness; and to praise Your name with the mouth of all who know You, and they shall bless You for all eternity.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 10 brings the anthropological-theological meditation to its climax. The three-fold refrain (10:4, 10:22, 10:31) is liturgically structured. The passage on divine control over speech (10:32-36) is philosophically extraordinary: God not only determined all events but literally fashioned every word before it was spoken.*
